results.title: Countable chain condition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A partial order $(P, \le)$ has the countable chain condition (c.c.c.) if every antichain of $P$ is countable, where an antichain is a set of pairwise incompatible elements: no two distinct members of it have a common lower bound in $P$.

results.title: σ-centered partial orders
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A partial order $P$ is $\sigma$-centered if there is a map $c : P \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, every finite set of elements $p$ with $c(p) = n$ has a common lower bound in $P$. Thus $P$ splits into countably many centered pieces $c^{-1}(n)$; the empty set is among the finite sets, so $P$ must be nonempty.

results.title: Martin's axiom for σ-centered partial orders
results.caption: Definition

Here $D \subseteq P$ is dense if every element of $P$ has an element of $D$ below it, and a filter is a nonempty upward closed subset of $P$ any…

results.title: Martin's axiom
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a cardinal $\kappa$, $\mathrm{MA}(\kappa)$ is the statement that for every partial order $P$ with the countable chain condition, every family $\mathcal{D}$ of at most $\kappa$ dense subsets of $P$ and every $p \in P$, there is a filter $G$ on $P$ with $p \in G$ that meets every member of $\mathcal{D}$. results.title: Coefficients of the unsigned Charlier polynomials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $m$, the coefficient of $x^m$ in the $n$-th unsigned Charlier polynomial of order $0$ over $\mathbb{N}$ equals the unsigned Charlier coefficient $c(n, m)$.

results.title: Zassenhaus conjecture on torsion units
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Kourovka 17.67 (H. Zassenhaus's conjecture, recorded by V. D. Mazurov): every unit of finite order of the integral group ring `ℤG` of a finite group `G` is conjugate, by a unit of the rational group ring `ℚG`, to an element `±g` with `g ∈ G`.

results.title: Counterexample to the first Zassenhaus conjecture (Kourovka 17.67)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist a finite group $G$ and a unit $u$ of finite order of the integral group ring $\mathbb{Z}G$ such that for every unit $v$ of the rational group ring $\mathbb{Q}G$, every $g \in G$ and every sign $\varepsilon \in \{1, -1\}$, the conjugate $v u v^{-1}$, computed in $\mathbb{Q}G$, is not equal to $\varepsilon g$. That is, the first Zassenhaus conjecture is false.

results.title: Degree of a finite extension of the reals
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $E$ is a field that is a finite-dimensional algebra over $\mathbb{R}$, then the dimension of $E$ as a real vector space is $1$ or $2$.

results.title: Galois groups over the reals have order 1 or 2
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $E$ is a finite Galois extension of $\mathbb{R}$, then the Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(E/\mathbb{R})$ has order $1$ or $2$.

results.title: Galois groups over the reals have order a power of 2
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $E$ is a finite Galois extension of $\mathbb{R}$, then the Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(E/\mathbb{R})$ has order $2^n$ for some natural number $n$.

results.title: Morita's p-adic gamma values at natural numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a prime $p$ and a natural number $n$, this is the $p$-adic integer $(-1)^n \prod_{0 < j < n,\ p \nmid j} j$: $(-1)^n$ times the product of the positive integers below $n$ that are not divisible by $p$. At $n = 0$ the product is empty and the value is $1$. These are the finite values that Morita's $p$-adic gamma function interpolates.

results.title: Morita's p-adic gamma function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a prime $p$, a continuous function $\Gamma : \mathbb{Z}_p \to \mathbb{Z}_p$ is a Morita $p$-adic gamma function when $\Gamma(0) = 1$, $\Gamma(n)$ equals Morita's finite value $(-1)^n \prod_{0 < j < n,\ p \nmid j} j$ for every positive integer $n$, and $\Gamma(x)$ is a unit of $\mathbb{Z}_p$ for every $x \in \mathbb{Z}_p$.

results.title: Existence and uniqueness of Morita's p-adic gamma function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every odd prime $p$ there is exactly one continuous function $\Gamma : \mathbb{Z}_p \to \mathbb{Z}_p$ that is a Morita $p$-adic gamma function, that is, $\Gamma(0) = 1$, $\Gamma(n) = (-1)^n \prod_{0 < j < n,\ p \nmid j} j$ for every positive integer $n$, and $\Gamma(x)$ is a unit of $\mathbb{Z}_p$ for every $x \in \mathbb{Z}_p$.

results.title: The Euclidean plane for discrete isometry groups
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: $E_2$ is the Euclidean plane: the real vector space $\mathbb{R}^2$ of pairs of real numbers with the standard Euclidean inner product and norm.

results.title: Isometry group of the Euclidean plane
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: $M_2$ is the group, under composition, of affine isometries of the Euclidean plane onto itself.

results.title: Linear part of a plane isometry
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The linear part of an affine isometry $f$ of the Euclidean plane is the linear isometry $A$ of the plane such that $f(x + v) = f(x) + A v$ for every point $x$ and every vector $v$.

results.title: Point group of a group of plane isometries
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The point group of a group $G$ of affine isometries of the Euclidean plane is the set of linear parts of the elements of $G$.

results.title: Translation lattice
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The translation lattice of a subgroup $G$ of the group $M_2$ of affine isometries of the Euclidean plane $E_2$ is the set of vectors $v \in E_2$ such that the translation $x \mapsto v + x$ belongs to $G$.

results.title: Translation homomorphism
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The group homomorphism from the additive group of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ (written multiplicatively) to the group of affine isometries of the plane that sends a vector $v$ to translation by $v$, the isometry $x \mapsto v + x$.

results.title: Translation lattice as an additive subgroup
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a group $G$ of affine isometries of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, the additive subgroup of $\mathbb{R}^2$ consisting of the vectors $v$ such that translation by $v$ belongs to $G$; it is the preimage of $G$ under the translation homomorphism $v \mapsto (x \mapsto v + x)$.

results.title: Membership in the translation lattice subgroup
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every group $G$ of affine isometries of the Euclidean plane and every vector $v$ of the plane, $v$ belongs to the translation lattice subgroup of $G$ if and only if $v$ belongs to the translation lattice of $G$.

results.title: Carrier of the translation lattice subgroup
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every group $G$ of affine isometries of the Euclidean plane, the underlying set of the translation lattice subgroup of $G$ is the translation lattice of $G$.

results.title: Translations are determined by their vectors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For vectors $v$ and $w$ of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, if translation by $v$ and translation by $w$ are the same affine isometry, then $v = w$. Equivalently, the translation homomorphism $v \mapsto (x \mapsto v + x)$ from the additive group of the plane to the group of affine isometries of the plane is injective.

results.title: Separation criterion for groups of plane isometries
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ of affine isometries of the Euclidean plane satisfies the separation criterion if there is $\varepsilon > 0$ such that every element $f \ne \mathrm{id}$ of $G$ whose linear part is the identity satisfies $\|f(0)\| \ge \varepsilon$, and every element $f$ of $G$ whose linear part $A$ is not the identity satisfies $\|A - I\| \ge \varepsilon$, where $I$ is the identity map and the norm is the operator norm.

Then the translation lattice of $G$, the additive subgroup of vectors $v$ such that…

results.title: Conjugating a translation by a plane isometry
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $g$ be an affine isometry of the Euclidean plane with linear part $A$, let $v$ be a vector, and write $\tau_w$ for translation by a vector $w$. Then $g \circ \tau_v \circ g^{-1} = \tau_{A v}$.

results.title: The point group preserves the translation lattice
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group of affine isometries of the Euclidean plane. If $A$ belongs to the point group of $G$, that is, $A$ is the linear part of some element of $G$, and $v$ belongs to the translation lattice of $G$, then $A v$ belongs to the translation lattice of $G$.

results.title: Classification of discrete additive subgroups of the plane
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every discrete additive subgroup `G` of `ℝ²` is trivial, cyclic (generated by a single nonzero vector), or a rank-two lattice (generated by two `ℝ`-linearly independent vectors).

results.title: Binary words in which both letters occur infinitely often
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An infinite word $w = \ell_0 \ell_1 \ell_2 \cdots$ over the letters $a$ and $b$ belongs to the set $\mathcal{W}$ when both letters occur infinitely often in it, that is, when there are infinitely many positions $i$ with $\ell_i = a$ and infinitely many positions $i$ with $\ell_i = b$.

results.title: Position function of a letter
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an infinite binary word $w = \ell_0 \ell_1 \cdots$, a letter $\alpha$ and $n \ge 1$, $p_\alpha(n)$ is the position of the $n$-th occurrence of $\alpha$ in $w$, counting positions from $0$; that is, $p_\alpha(n)$ is the $n$-th smallest index $i$ with $\ell_i = \alpha$.

results.title: Relative position function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $w = \ell_0 \ell_1 \ell_2 \cdots$ be an infinite word over $\{a, b\}$, and for a letter $\alpha$ and $n \ge 1$ let $p_\alpha(n)$ be the position (counting from $0$) of the $n$-th occurrence of $\alpha$ in $w$, or $0$ if $\alpha$ occurs fewer than $n$ times. The relative position function of $w$ is the integer-valued function $r(n) = p_b(n) - p_a(n)$, $n \ge 1$.

results.title: Position of the first occurrence of the initial letter
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If an infinite binary word $w$ starts with the letter $\alpha$, then the first occurrence of $\alpha$ in $w$ is at position $0$, that is, $p_\alpha(1) = 0$.

results.title: Relative position of a word starting with $ab$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If an infinite word $w$ over $\{a, b\}$ starts with $ab$, then its relative position function satisfies $r(1) = 1$.

results.title: Monotone 3-SAT instances
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A monotone 3-SAT instance is a pair $(n, \varphi)$ of a natural number $n$, the number of variables, and a CNF formula $\varphi$.

results.title: Well-formed monotone 3-SAT instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A monotone 3-SAT instance $(n, \varphi)$ is well formed when every clause of the CNF formula $\varphi$ is a list of exactly three literals (repetitions allowed), each with a variable below $n$, and the literals of each clause are all positive or all negative.

results.title: Satisfiable monotone 3-SAT instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A monotone 3-SAT instance $(n, \varphi)$ is feasible when there is a list of $n$ truth values $a_0, \dots, a_{n-1}$ such that the assignment sending each variable $x < n$ to $a_x$ and every variable $x \ge n$ to false satisfies the CNF formula $\varphi$.
